grh_36a6e0b55af9683ab120.title: Mc Guffey's Hong Kong Connection
paragraphs: Drug-enforcement agents Arnold McGuffey and Miss Tawawa travel to Hong Kong to break a heroin-smuggling route, beginning with an airline emergency in which Tawawa helps land a jet after the flight crew is incapacitated. McGuffey dismisses her suspicion that a doll factory is part of the operation, but she takes a job there and discovers that selected dolls are packed with heroin. McGuffey finally follows the same trail, walks into the smugglers' trap and is rescued when Tawawa ignores his order to stay behind. The Hong Kong police take the traffickers, and McGuffey is forced to admit that his partner's hunch was right before their boss assigns the pair to another narcotics case in Hollywood.

grh_3622d7b4b3b298b5ac47.title: Words at War 44-01-04 (30) They Shall Inherit the Earth
paragraphs: A dramatization based on Otto Zoff's They Shall Inherit the Earth examines what modern war has done to children in different countries. Scenes contrast ordinary childhood play with militarization, hunger, displacement, bombing and the emotional damage suffered by children in Europe and elsewhere. The program ends with a promise that the adults who survive must feed, find and protect the young, while teaching them enough trust in other people to inherit a world less governed by fear and war.

grh_369b5873d2d69c3c1752.title: Science at War
paragraphs: A documentary-style adaptation of George W. Gray's Science at War asks whether scientific progress is responsible for modern destruction or merely a tool shaped by human choices. Through dramatized examples involving poison gas, magnetic mines, mine detectors, battlefield medicine and wartime engineering, it shows science creating weapons and also countering them or saving lives. The program concludes that knowledge cannot simply be reversed and that humanity must decide whether scientific power will serve war or a shared peaceful future.
